name: TAOP adversarial agent-reputation pattern dataset
description: Documented adversarial patterns against agent-reputation and adjacent trust systems, grouped by the three benchmark attack classes: sybil_farming, slow_burn_harvest, collusive_ring. Entries describe the pattern, the on-chain signals a defender can observe, and the mitigations that apply. Sources are cited conservatively; entries marked confidence=medium/low are industry-reported or academic analogs rather than measured incidents in agent-reputation systems.

attackClasses.sybil_farming: Many cheap identities manufacture reputation without tasks of value.
attackClasses.slow_burn_harvest: A single identity accumulates reputation slowly, then extracts once.
attackClasses.collusive_ring: A group of identities mutually inflate each other's reputation.

patterns.title: Classic Sybil identity multiplication
patterns.description: An adversary creates many identities that are not tied to distinct real-world principals and uses them to gain influence in a reputation or voting system.
onChainSignals: many accounts funded from one source
low per-account activity outside the reputation program
patterns.realWorldEvidence: The foundational formal analysis of Sybil attacks establishes that identity creation is cheap without a central authority or a costly identity primitive.

patterns.title: Sybil farming of self-attested completions
patterns.description: Fresh identities self-attest large numbers of completions with no verifier in the loop, converting transaction fees into apparent reputation.
onChainSignals: bursts of attestations from new accounts
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Early empirical work on permissionless agent-reputation registries reports weak grounding and substantial Sybil behaviour in feedback data.

patterns.title: Airdrop farming with disposable wallets
patterns.description: Farmers split activity across hundreds of wallets to satisfy per-identity eligibility thresholds, then consolidate rewards.
onChainSignals: funding graphs converging on a few hubs
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Widely documented in incentive-program analyses across ecosystems; identity-per-wallet assumptions repeatedly failed.

sources.title: Industry analyses of token distribution farming

mitigations: sybil-resistant eligibility (proof of personhood, staking with lockups)

patterns.title: Social-graph Sybil defenses fail on sparse or adversarial graphs
patterns.description: Defenses that rely on the honest region of a social graph being fast-mixing can be defeated when attackers establish believable edges or when the graph is sparse.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Analyses of social-network Sybil defenses show limited guarantees against adversaries who can create or buy edges.

sources.title: SybilGuard: Defending Against Sybil Attacks via Social Networks
An Analysis of Social Network-Based Sybil Defenses

patterns.title: Sybil-resilient voting via per-user tickets (SumUp)
patterns.description: Content-voting systems resist Sybil votes by giving each user a vote credit per item that is weighted by the voter's global influence; bought votes collapse toward zero weight.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: SumUp demonstrates practical Sybil resilience without identity verification by tuning per-user influence.

patterns.title: Identity cost inversion under subsidized fees
patterns.description: When transaction fees are subsidized or refunded, identity creation and activity become free, collapsing any fee-based Sybil resistance.
onChainSignals: fee payer accounts distinct from actors
rent refunds recycled into new accounts
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Observed in fee-subsidy programs where farming cost fell to zero; protocol subsidies are routinely farmed.
mitigations: charge identity-storage rent that is not refundable to the actor
bond capital that is slashable, not refundable

patterns.title: Sockpuppet accounts in moderated platforms
patterns.description: Operators of multiple accounts use them to amplify content or evade sanctions while appearing independent.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Public arbitration cases and platform integrity reports document long-running sockpuppet investigations.

sources.title: Platform integrity and arbitration case records

patterns.title: Cross-account score laundering
patterns.description: High-reputation accounts are retired and their reputation, capabilities, or credentials are transferred to fresh accounts, defeating per-identity reset penalties.
onChainSignals: sudden inactivity followed by mirror activity
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Analogous to aged-account and credential-resale markets documented across platforms.
mitigations: reputation attached to work products with provenance

patterns.title: Sybil amplification of challenge outcomes
patterns.description: An attacker uses many identities to overwhelm the resolver with frivolous challenges or to coordinate mass-false disputes against a competitor.
onChainSignals: challenges with empty or duplicated evidence URIs
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Griefing-by-volume is a standard denial-of-service pattern for adjudicated systems.

sources.title: Denial of service via adjudication volume

mitigations: bonded challenges that are forfeited when rejected

patterns.title: Stake rental (capital as a service)
patterns.description: Attackers rent staked capital for the duration of an attack instead of owning it, reducing the effective cost of stake-gated mechanisms to a rental fee.
onChainSignals: stake delegation concentrated around attack windows
stake returned immediately after score use
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Observed in staking and validator economies where delegation is liquid; also explored in flash-loan governance literature.
mitigations: score that decays immediately on unstake

patterns.title: Sybil resistance by proof-of-work identity puzzles
patterns.description: Puzzles raise the marginal cost of each identity; attackers respond by amortizing solver hardware, converting identity cost into compute cost.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Compute-based identity costs shift but do not eliminate Sybil incentives when the attacker values scale.

patterns.title: Reputation bootstrap as a paid service
patterns.description: Service providers sell pre-built reputation, including attestation packages and 'aged' agent profiles, removing the need for the attacker to run the farm.
onChainSignals: capability registrations batched from few funders
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Markets for reviews, followers, and account history repeatedly emerge wherever reputation has economic value.
mitigations: require unique work products with provenance

patterns.title: Beanstalk governance flash-loan accumulation
patterns.description: An attacker accumulated governance power, then executed a single proposal that drained the protocol in one transaction.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Widely reported April 2022 governance exploit with roughly 182 million USD in losses.
mitigations: value caps gated by bonded capital

patterns.title: Oracle manipulation after position buildup
patterns.description: An attacker builds a position slowly, then manipulates a reference price to liquidate or borrow against inflated collateral in a single block.
onChainSignals: price deviation in a single slot
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Mango Markets incident, October 2022, with roughly 114 million USD involved.

patterns.title: Rug-pull credibility accumulation
patterns.description: Operators build credibility for months, then drain liquidity or revoke service in a single exit event.
onChainSignals: long quiet period before a large withdrawal
unlock schedule clustered with deployment of new contracts
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Extensively documented in cryptoasset fraud analyses across 2021-2023.

patterns.title: Power-seller trust-then-scam
patterns.description: A seller accumulates high ratings over years, then fulfills a burst of high-value orders fraudulently before disappearing.
onChainSignals: stable history followed by order-value spike
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Long-documented marketplace fraud pattern; consumer protection reporting on 'power seller' scams.
mitigations: escrow sized to outstanding order value

patterns.title: Aged-domain abuse pipeline
patterns.description: Domains are aged to accumulate trust signals, then repurposed for phishing or malware distribution in a single campaign.
onChainSignals: reputation history unrelated to new content
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Standard finding in email and web security: domain age is a weak trust signal because it is purchasable.
mitigations: require continuous activity rather than age

patterns.title: Insider sleeper behavior in agent pipelines
patterns.description: An agent behaves correctly for many episodes, then triggers a damaging action once it is trusted with higher privileges.
onChainSignals: rare action types late in a history
score plateau followed by one high-impact action
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Model backdoor research shows that deceptive behavior can survive long benign training periods.

sources.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training

patterns.title: Loan-to-value drift before default
patterns.description: A borrower gradually increases leverage and withdraws collateral until a small adverse move leaves bad debt.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Recurring postmortem theme in lending protocol incident reports.

patterns.title: Aged-account resale after reputation build
patterns.description: Accounts with accumulated reputation are sold to buyers who then perform high-value abuse with inherited trust.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Aged-account markets are a persistent feature of platform trust and safety reporting.

patterns.title: Bounty-program trust exploitation
patterns.description: A contributor builds a record of valid reports, then submits a high-severity report that is actually a self-serving exploit or false alarm at a critical moment.
onChainSignals: reports that benefit the reporter's positions
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Discussed in security community retrospectives on insider risk in disclosure programs.

patterns.title: Time-delayed attack in reputation systems
patterns.description: The adversary waits for the system's trust to mature, then defects once; the long honest period is the camouflage.
onChainSignals: long faithful histories that end abruptly
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Classic result in repeated-game trust analysis: with a long enough horizon, trusting based on history alone is exploitable.

sources.title: A survey of attack and defense techniques for reputation systems

patterns.title: Mutual review rings on marketplaces
patterns.description: A closed group of sellers buys and reviews each other's products to manufacture top-rated placement.
onChainSignals: high reciprocity between a small set of accounts
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Consumer-protection enforcement actions and platform integrity reports on incentivized fake reviews.

patterns.title: Collusion in open-collaboration reputation
patterns.description: Reputation formulas without collusion resistance reward cliques that rate each other; the paper formalizes manipulation resistance requirements.
onChainSignals: clique structure in the rating graph
score inflation uncorrelated with external outcomes
patterns.realWorldEvidence: de Alfaro et al. analyze manipulation-resistance properties of reputation systems for open collaboration.

patterns.title: Sybil-ring score inflation
patterns.description: Attackers combine Sybil identity creation with mutual rating so that each identity appears to have distinct, satisfied counterparties.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Empirical feedback analysis in early agent-reputation registries reports exactly this combination.

patterns.title: Reciprocity bias in hospitality reviews
patterns.description: Hosts and guests rate each other highly to preserve mutual access, producing inflated symmetric scores without explicit coordination.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Hospitality platforms moved to simultaneous review reveal specifically to reduce reciprocity bias.

sources.title: Platform design responses to reciprocity bias

patterns.title: Endorsement exchange groups
patterns.description: Professional networks are gamed by groups that exchange endorsements for unrelated skills.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Long-standing industry observation in professional networking platforms.

patterns.title: App-store review exchange pods
patterns.description: Developer pods download and review each other's apps to climb rankings, occasionally with coordinated keyword stuffing.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Documented in platform integrity reporting and press investigations.

patterns.title: Cartel formation in peer grading
patterns.description: Participants in peer-graded environments collude to award each other high marks, degrading the grading signal.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Studied in educational peer-assessment literature; remedied with adjudication and calibration.

patterns.title: Governance vote-buying rings
patterns.description: A coalition coordinates voting power, sometimes paying for delegation, to pass proposals that benefit the coalition.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Documented across DAO governance studies and on-chain analyses of delegation markets.

patterns.title: Chip-dumping collusion in games
patterns.description: Colluding players deliberately transfer value to each other in games of skill, converting coordinated play into a wealth transfer.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Well documented in online poker security practice; the same structure applies to any skill-based wager.

patterns.title: Collaborative score farming in agent swarms
patterns.description: A swarm of agents operated by one principal completes trivial 'tasks' for each other and cross-attests, creating the appearance of diverse demand.
onChainSignals: task types with no external consumers
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Extrapolated from feedback-manipulation findings in permissionless registries.

patterns.title: Rating-ring detection evasion via slow rotation
patterns.description: Rings rotate membership slowly so static graph detectors see evolving, apparently diverse neighborhoods.
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Anti-fraud literature notes that adaptive rings defeat one-shot graph snapshots.

patterns.title: Task-issuer collusion with attestation issuers
patterns.description: Where attestations require a counterparty signature, the counterparty is itself controlled by the attestee, so the 'proof of interaction' is vacuous.
onChainSignals: counterparty accounts funded by the attestee
patterns.realWorldEvidence: Common in attestation systems that accept any counterparty signature without independence checks.
